in_greek.name: Λεοντία
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Λεοντία σημαίνει θηλυκή μορφή του Λέων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λεοντία προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη Λέων, που σημαίνει λιοντάρι ή καρδιά. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της γενναιότητας και της πίστης. Οι χριστιανοί γονείς επέλεξαν αυτό το όνομα για τις κόρες τους για να εκφράσουν την ελπίδα και την προστασία που προσφέρει ο Θεός.

historical_references.reference: The martyred Saint Leoncia of Bergamo is believed to have lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century. According to legend, she was the daughter of a Roman nobleman and was betrothed to a man against her will. Leoncia feigned madness in order to escape the arranged marriage and was sent to a distant estate. There, she dedicated herself to Christ and performed various acts of charity. Eventually, she was discovered and brought back to Bergamo. Despite torture and threats, she confessed her faith and was executed along with her servant, Celsion.

Saint Leoncia of Tripoli, also known as Saint Leoncia of Byzantium, was a Christian martyr from the city of Tripoli in Libya. She is believed to have lived during the 3rd century. According to legend, Leoncia was a wealthy and beautiful woman who converted to Christianity and dedicated herself to helping the poor. She was denounced to the Roman authorities and was tortured and imprisoned. Despite her suffering, she refused to recant her faith. She was eventually executed, along with her servant, Fortunata.
